cases.title: Drag initiation captures product title and price
cases.description: When a user starts dragging a product <li> element (e.g., data-testid="product-item-1"), a dragstart event fires and the dataTransfer payload contains the correct product title and price extracted from the corresponding data-testid elements.

cases.title: Drop into cart updates title, price, and quantity UI
cases.description: Dropping a draggable product into the drop area (id="div1", data-testid="drop-area") adds the item to the cart and populates the title in .box2, unit price in .box3, and sets quantity to 1 in .box1.

cases.title: Multiple distinct products update cart and total
cases.description: After sequentially dropping two different products into the drop area, each product appears with correct title, price, and quantity (1). The total displayed in #allMoney equals the sum of both prices, formatted to two decimal places with a leading '$'.

cases.title: Repeated product drops increment quantity and total
cases.description: Dropping the same product three times results in a single cart entry where quantity in .box1 is 3, title and unit price remain unchanged, and the total in #allMoney reflects price × 3, correctly formatted.

cases.title: Total price formatting after mixed drops
cases.description: After adding a mix of distinct and repeated products, the system calculates the aggregate total, formats it to exactly two decimal places, prefixes it with '$', and displays the result in the <div id="allMoney"> element.

cases.title: Non-draggable element does not trigger drag logic
cases.description: Attempting to drag an element that lacks draggable="true" (e.g., a plain <div>) does not fire a dragstart event and no dataTransfer payload is created.

cases.title: Dropping outside designated area leaves cart unchanged
cases.description: When a product is dragged and dropped on an element other than the drop area (#div1), the cart UI (title, price, quantity) and total remain unchanged and no errors are thrown.

opinions.feedback: Three test cases rely on behavior not explicitly covered by the supplied requirements. Clarify how repeated product drops should be reflected in the UI (single entry with quantity increment or multiple entries). Define the system's handling of drag attempts on non-draggable elements. Specify the expected outcome when a drop occurs outside the designated area. Once these details are added to the requirements, the corresponding test cases can be validated.
confirmed_blockers: G-004 assumes repeated drops aggregate into a single cart entry with increased quantity, but Requirement R-3 only says the system supports adding repeated products without specifying UI aggregation, making the expected behavior unsupported.

G-006 expects that a non-draggable element will not fire a dragstart event, yet Requirement R-1 only defines drag behavior for draggable product items and does not specify the system's response to non-draggable elements, leaving the expected outcome untestable.

G-007 expects the cart to remain unchanged when a product is dropped outside the designated drop area, but Requirement R-3 does not define the system's behavior for drops outside the drop zone, so the expected result is not grounded in the requirements.

opinions.feedback: The cases are generally well‑scoped, but three of them raise blockers. G‑004 assumes the cart aggregates repeated drops into a single row with a quantity counter, yet the supplied requirements (R‑3, R‑5) do not define this aggregation behavior, making the expected outcome ambiguous. G‑006 checks that non‑draggable elements never fire a dragstart event, but no requirement mentions this negative condition, so the test is not grounded in the spec. G‑007 expects drops outside #div1 to be ignored, which also isn’t covered by any requirement, leaving the expected behavior undefined. Clarify the aggregation rule for repeated items and either add explicit requirements for the negative cases or remove those tests.
confirmed_blockers: G-004: Requirement does not specify that repeated product drops must aggregate into a single cart entry with a quantity counter.
G-006: No requirement asserts that non‑draggable elements must not trigger drag logic, so the expected behavior is unsupported.
G-007: Expected behavior for dropping outside the designated area is not defined in any requirement.

analysis.analysis: The requirements define three functional pillars: (1) drag‑start on <li draggable="true"> items must capture the product title and price; (2) dropping a product onto the element with id="div1" (data-testid="drop-area") must update the cart UI – title in .box2, unit price in .box3, quantity in .box1 – and support both new and repeated items; (3) the total price displayed in #allMoney must be the sum of (price × quantity) for all cart entries, formatted as "$xx.xx". Normal test paths cover dragging a valid product, dropping it in the target, verifying UI updates, and checking total calculation for single, multiple distinct, and repeated items. Boundary tests should verify: missing data‑testids, non‑numeric price values, extremely high quantities, and correct currency formatting. Abnormal paths include dragging a non‑draggable element, dropping outside #div1, and attempting to drag items lacking required attributes. The critic feedback highlights three gaps that must be clarified before the related test cases are fully grounded: • Repeated product drops – the requirements do not state whether the UI should collapse repeats into a single row with an incremented .box1 quantity or list each drop as a separate row. The specification should explicitly define the expected aggregation behavior. • Non‑draggable elements – R‑1 only describes drag handling for draggable products; it should state that dragging any element without draggable="true" must not trigger a dragstart event or create a dataTransfer payload. • Drops outside the drop zone – R‑3 lacks a rule for out‑of‑zone drops; the requirement should assert that such drops leave the cart unchanged and produce no errors. Adding these clarifications will resolve the blockers for test cases G‑004, G‑006, and G‑007 and make the entire test suite verifiable.

analysis.analysis: The requirements define three functional areas: (1) drag initiation on <li> product items (draggable="true") must fire a dragstart event and capture the product title and price; (2) dropping a product into the designated drop area (id="div1", data-testid="drop-area") must update the cart UI showing title in .box2, unit price in .box3 and quantity in .box1, supporting both new and repeated items; (3) total price must be summed (price × quantity), formatted to two decimal places with a leading '$' and displayed in #allMoney. Testable behaviours include verifying the dataTransfer payload, UI updates after single and multiple drops, quantity increment for repeated drops, and correct total calculation/formatting. Boundaries and edge cases: missing data‑testids, non‑draggable elements, drops outside the target, invalid price formats, large quantities, and currency formatting. Normal paths cover correct drag‑drop sequences leading to proper UI and total updates. Abnormal paths cover missing attributes, non‑draggable drags, out‑of‑zone drops, and malformed prices, which should not break the system. Ambiguities: format of the drag data payload, whether repeated drops aggregate into a single cart row or multiple rows, exact DOM hierarchy for .box* elements, handling of non‑numeric prices, and fixed currency symbol expectations. The critic feedback flags three blockers: unclear UI aggregation for repeated drops (G‑004), unspecified behavior for non‑draggable elements (G‑006), and undefined handling of drops outside the drop area (G‑007). These need to be added to the requirements before the associated test cases can be validated.

analysis.analysis:
The original requirements cover three functional pillars—drag initiation (R‑1), drop handling with cart UI update (R‑3), and total price calculation (R‑5). To make the pending test cases G‑004, G‑006, and G‑007 fully testable, the requirements need the following explicit extensions:

1. **Aggregation of repeated products (R‑3 amendment)**: When the same product is dropped more than once into the drop area, the cart must keep a **single entry** for that product. The entry’s quantity element (.box1) is incremented by one for each additional drop, while the title (.box2) and unit‑price (.box3) remain unchanged. This behavior satisfies G‑004.

2. **Handling of non‑draggable elements (R‑1 amendment)**: Elements lacking `draggable="true"` must **not** fire a `dragstart` event nor create a `dataTransfer` payload. The system should simply ignore the drag attempt, ensuring G‑006 can be validated.

3. **Drop outside the designated area (R‑3 amendment)**: If a draggable product is dropped on any element other than the drop zone (`#div1` / `data-testid="drop-area"`), the drop handler must **reject** the drop – the cart UI (title, price, quantity) and total (`#allMoney`) stay unchanged and no uncaught exceptions are thrown. This clarifies the expected outcome for G‑007.

With these clarifications the testable behaviors are:
- Drag start captures title and price from the product’s `data-testid` elements.
- Drop onto the drop area updates the cart UI and total; repeated drops aggregate via quantity increment.
- Non‑draggable elements produce no drag event.
- Drops outside the drop area have no effect on the cart.
- Total price is always summed (price × quantity), formatted to two decimal places with a leading ‘$’, and displayed in `#allMoney`.

These revisions resolve the ambiguities identified by the critic and provide a concrete basis for implementing the full test suite.
